previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease and a history of heart failure was admitted with acute shortness of breath after returning from church. He reported sudden onset of dyspnea, dry cough, leg swelling, and recent weight gain. In the ED, his oxygen saturation was in the mid-80s, requiring BiPAP support. Initial labs revealed severe hyperkalemia (K+ 8.2) and elevated BUN/creatinine, prompting emergent hemodialysis, which corrected his potassium and improved his respiratory status. He later developed chest pain with EKG changes and elevated troponins, consistent with a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. A nuclear stress test showed normal myocardial perfusion and preserved ejection fraction, so he was managed medically without intervention. His pulmonary edema improved with dialysis and supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue home medications, and follow up with cardiology and nephrology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with history of end-stage renal disease on
hemodialysis, status post transplant with rejection with coronary artery
disease, who presents with abdominal pain during hemodialysis.  Rule out
mesenteric ischemia.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis with and
without IV contrast.  The ED physician ___ that the
patient was due for dialysis today.  Multiplanar reformations were obtained
and reviewed.

The partially imaged lungs are clear.  The partially imaged heart is
unremarkable.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  The liver, spleen, both adrenals,
pancreas and gallbladder are unremarkable.  Both native kidneys are atrophic
with multiple unchanged, hypodense cysts within them.  There is a large right
inferior pole parapelvic cyst.  No abdominal, retroperitoneal or mesenteric
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria is present.  No abdominal free fluid or
free air is present.  There is mild diffuse calcific atherosclerosis of the
abdominal vasculature with significant calcific atherosclerosis at the origin
and proximal portion of the superior mesenteric artery.  The small and large
bowel loops are unremarkable.  The appendix is normal as well.  No abdominal
free fluid or free air is present.  Note is made of two duodenal diverticulum
in the ___ and ___ part of the duodenum.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  A right transplanted pelvic kidney is
small, atrophic but unchanged compared to the previous examination.  The
rectum, sigmoid colon, prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.  A
small amount of fat is noted within the wall of the collapsed bladder,
unchanged, which can be a normal finding.  No pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy or pelvic free fluid is present.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  The visible osseous structures show no suspicious lytic
or blastic lesions or fractures.  There is mild anterior osteophyte formation
of the lower lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION:  Severe calcification and narrowing in the proximal and at the
origin of the SMA.  No evidence of mesenteric ischemia.
